contract: POST /api/libraries/:id/scan is the admin library scan: an admin who can access the library gets 200 and the scan runs asynchronously, updating libraries.lastScan and lastScanVersion and persisting the metadata precedence snapshot on completion; ?force=1 rescans even unchanged items; unauthenticated, non-admin, inaccessible-library and unknown-library requests are rejected without a scan.
evidence: go-backend/testmachine/scenarios/scan: 6 upstream scenarios, all passing in two consecutive full packet runs
exceptions: Historical evidence leads retained for provenance: go-backend/testmachine/contracts/parity/full-suite-report.json#library-scan-rerun.
The 200 response body is the reason phrase Express sends for sendStatus(200); clients do not read it, so scenarios assert the status only.

invariants.contract: The route exists at POST /api/libraries/:id/scan and is admin-only: an anonymous request answers 401, a non-admin 403, an admin without access to that library 403 from the middleware and an unknown library id 404; no rejected request runs a scan or moves libraries.lastScan, and the item rows stay unchanged.

An accepted scan answers 200 and runs asynchronously; when it completes it moves libraries.lastScan strictly forward, writes lastScanVersion 2.37.2 and extraData.lastScanMetadataPrecedence, without changing the ids, relative paths, titles or own lastScan stamps of items whose files did not change (also on a repeat scan), and a scan after a new book folder appears adds exactly that one item.

A plain scan skips items without file changes, so an edited metadata/items/<id>/metadata.json is not reread; the web client always sends the force query (client/store/libraries.js:76) and only the exact value ?force=1 on its own rescans every item (req.query.force === '1'), so ?force=0 behaves as a plain scan and ?force=1 applies and rewrites the edited sidecar.
